subject: Request: QuantaBio latency SLO carveout + early-payment discount
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: QuantaBio latency SLO carveout + early-payment discount

Team — quick escalation. QuantaBio (contact: Erin Walsh / Sanjay Patel) asked for two non-standard items to close a pilot-to-paid expansion:

1) Latency SLO carveout: for the embeddings batch endpoint used in their high-throughput analytics pipeline, they want p95 increased from our standard 150ms to 400ms for a 90-day onboarding pilot window, with the understanding we will not assess credits for transient misses during that pilot.

2) Commercial concession: 10% early-payment discount if they pay net-15 on the first 6 invoices (they want this to offset their integration costs).

They are sensitive to price and want to sign this week. Legal flagged the SLO change as "material" and asked for exec sign-off on any variance to uptime/latency terms. I attached a first-pass SLO amendment and a deal summary (attaching below).

My ask: can I get an exec-level thumbs-up (Jonas/Marissa) to proceed with a guarded carveout plus a capped remedy schedule, and approval to offer the early-pay discount in return for a 6-month prepay or an equal revenue commitment? Specifics I propose below so we have something precise to put in DocuSign: 

- Pilot window: 90 days from production cutover.
- Temporary latency p95 threshold: 400ms for embeddings-batch endpoint only; all other endpoints unchanged.
- Uptime target: remain at 99.95% for control plane; customer accepts 99.8% for the piloted endpoint only.
- Remedies: credits limited to a maximum of one month of fees for the affected endpoint during the pilot (approx $12,000 cap) OR service credits capped at 5% of monthly invoice (whichever is lower).
- Monitoring: we provide a shared Grafana view and weekly synthetic test reports.
- Commercial: 10% discount if QuantaBio prepays the next 6 invoices (or signs a 6-month minimum committed spend).

Files attached: QuantaBio_SLO_Amendment_Draft.pdf; QuantaBio_Deal_Summary.xlsx; Synthetic-Test-Plan.md.

Connor
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0136

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: QuantaBio latency SLO carveout + early-payment discount

Connor — thanks for the clear ask and the draft. I read the SLO amendment and have a few edits/safeguards before I can greenlight:

- Credit cap: prefer 5% of invoice OR $10,000 cap (we should choose the lower number) for the pilot window. Keeps commercial exposure predictable.
- Sunset clause: automatic rollback of the carveout at day 91 unless customer signs standard terms or we agree a new amendment.
- Telemetry: require they onboard our synthetic checks and agree to a readiness checklist; if they refuse telemetry, we cannot accept a carveout.
- Exclusion: carveout limited to the embeddings-batch path only (not real-time or chat endpoints).

On the discount: 10% is acceptable if it's tied to a prepay or irrevocable ACH within 15 days. If they want net-15 without prepay, we should reduce discount to 5%.

I'll run this by Legal but I can escalate to Jonas for exec sign-off now. Attaching marked-up SLO amendment.

—Marissa
Senior Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: QuantaBio_SLO_Amendment_Draft.pdf (marked-up)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Request: QuantaBio latency SLO carveout + early-payment discount

Connor / Marissa — conditional approval from me. Two conditions I want in the DocuSign:

1) The carveout is explicitly time-boxed (90-day pilot) and auto-reverts unless we execute a permanent amendment.
2) Monitoring and alerting: Redwood must have read-only access to their telemetry and we must retain the right to terminate the carveout early if we observe production-impacting variance.

Also cap the total service-credit exposure (Marissa's suggestion OK). No precedent for making this permanent — we should track this as a one-off and log as a precedent request in Deal Desk.

Jonas
VP, Revenue Operations
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Hi Erin / Sanjay — forwarding the agreed guardrails from our side; we've got conditional exec sign-off pending Legal's quick review. Please see the attached SLO amendment (marked) and the deal summary.

Key points in our proposal (finalizing for DocuSign):
- 90-day pilot latency carveout for embeddings-batch endpoint only (p95 up to 400ms).
- Uptime status for that path set at 99.8% for the pilot; control plane stays at standard 99.95%.
- Remedies capped at the lower of 5% of monthly invoice or $10,000 for the pilot window.
- Redwood provides a shared Grafana dashboard and weekly synthetic test reports.
- 10% early-payment discount if QuantaBio prepays the next 6 invoices (or executes a 6-month committed spend). If you choose net-15 without prepay, discount reduces to 5%.

If this works, please confirm which commercial route you prefer (prepay vs net-15) and we'll send DocuSign with the final SLO amendment. DocuSign link will be: https://www.docusign.com/secure/txn/ABC-123-QUANTABIO
